articles.title: How Low Can PG&E Stock Go When The Risk Is Its Own?
articles.content: How Low Can PG&E Stock Go When The Risk Is Its Own? Trefis Team Tue, September 22, 2026 at 12:53 PM PDT 3 min read PCG ^GSPC SPGI NEE DUK Image from Pixabay PG&E (PCG) trades at about $12.94, the bottom of its 52-week range and about 32% below its high. Over the past twelve months it lost 12.2% while the S&P 500 gained 18.5%. That gap did not come from a market crash. And in market shocks since 2007, its deepest fall includes a one-day break in PG&E's own price data. What Has Changed For PG&E Since July? PG&E serves customers across Northern and Central California. Its investment case has rested on a $73 billion capital plan through 2030 that management said needs no new equity. But the CFO said in July that the plan is premised on a constructive legislative outcome on wildfire liability. The CEO went further. If the wildfire liability framework stayed unresolved or insufficient, the company would reevaluate its capital allocation priorities. The CEO would not say what that would look like. In early September, PG&E said it would invest $11.4 billion in California in 2027 after deferring $2 billion of planned spending, and launch a strategic review of its business and financing. The plan management reaffirmed in July is now under review. Is PG&E's Business Actually Getting Worse? Not on its own numbers. Revenue over the trailing twelve months is $25.84 billion, up 5.7%, in line with its 3-year average growth rate of 5.2%. The operating margin is 20.0%, above its 3-year average of 16.8%. The grid is also safer: the CEO says PG&E is in its fourth year with no major fires linked to its equipment. The CFO says rating agency S&P upgraded its credit rating to one notch below investment grade, citing progress in reducing wildfire risk. Management puts its data center pipeline at over 12 gigawatts. None of that settles who pays when a wildfire does happen . That is decided by the state legislature in Sacramento, and the company's plan depends on the answer. How Much Further Could PG&E Stock Fall In A Market Shock? Across 15 market shocks since 2007, PG&E fell an average of 19% peak to trough, against 16% for the S&P 500. A crash has usually hit it about as hard as the market. The deepest clean case was the 2020 COVID-19 crash, when it fell 59% while the index fell 34%. The deepest catalogued fall was 85%, from October 2018 to January 2019, while the index fell 19%. That window holds a one-day break in PG&E's price, either a collapse or a corporate separation, so it is not a clean read of a market shock. The stock is still about 73% below its high from before that window. Sized at 10% of a portfolio, that worst 85% fall would have cut about 9% of the whole. Story Continues Most recoveries have been quick. Of the falls it has fully recovered from, the median climb from the low back to the prior high took about 2 months. The exception was COVID, which took about 40 months. So a market shock is a risk you can size, though not always one you can wait out quickly. The one fall that never healed ran through PG&E's own price break, and with its plan under review, position size is what a holder controls. Could You Hold PG&E While Its Plan Is Under Review? It turns on size more than nerve. How much of your money sits in this one utility? What would you sell if the review went badly? Weighing that across many holdings is the job our High Quality Portfolio does. And if the lower price is what tempts you, our Dip Buyer's Playbook ranks which fallen names have the fundamentals to recover. articles.title: ABM Industries (ABM) Is Scaling in Semiconductors and Data Centers. What Is Holding the Stock Back?
articles.content: ABM Industries (ABM) Is Scaling in Semiconductors and Data Centers. What Is Holding the Stock Back? Faheem Tahir Tue, September 22, 2026 at 1:22 PM PDT 5 min read ABM On September 8, 2026, ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM) reported financial results for its fiscal third quarter, the three months ended July 31, 2026. Revenue reached a company record of $2.3 billion, up 4.2% from a year earlier, and adjusted earnings per diluted share rose 27% to $1.04. Nine-month free cash flow totaled $199.6 million, compared with $42.4 million over the same stretch last year. Management raised the midpoint of its full-year adjusted earnings guidance to a range of $3.95 to $4.10 per share and increased its full-year free cash flow forecast to approximately $210 million. ABM Industries (ABM): Three Analysts Raised Targets, None Moved Off Hold A Cleveland-Cliffs facility in the Industrial Valley. Photo from Cleveland-Cliffs Bulls: Faster Deleveraging and a Fast-Scaling Semiconductor and Data Center Business Give Analysts Reason to Raise Targets Deutsche Bank lifted its price target on ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM) to $54 from $52 on September 9, 2026, maintaining a Hold rating, pointing to the company's progress in its higher-growth business lines. Baird's Andrew Wittmann raised his target to $53 from $48 the same day, keeping a Neutral rating, and noted in his updated model that several parts of the business are trending favorably even as competitive pressure persists elsewhere. Truist raised its target to $49 from $45 on September 14, 2026, keeping a Hold rating, attributing the stock's recent outperformance to a mix of solid results, an improved guidance picture, and rising recognition of ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM)'s growth-oriented segments, though the firm said its neutral stance reflects what it called a "light catalyst path" for the shares. The underlying business supports the optimism behind those target increases. ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM)'s revenue tied to semiconductor facilities, microgrids, and data centers totaled close to $775 million over the first nine months of the fiscal year, now topping 11% of total revenue, with organic growth in the semiconductor business alone running at 65%. CEO Scott Salmirs described the company's recent purchase of WGNSTAR as extending ABM's reach from working around semiconductor fabrication facilities to operating directly inside them. Manufacturing and distribution revenue climbed 18% to $481 million, aviation revenue rose 12% to $328.1 million on the back of continued growth at its London Heathrow contract, and strong cash generation helped it reach its sub-3-times leverage target a full quarter earlier than planned. ABM also secured a new $300 million receivables financing facility to diversify its funding sources. Story Continues Bears: Three Analysts Raised Targets Without Raising Ratings, and the Weaker Segments Explain Why None of the three cautious analysts highlighted here moved off a Hold or Neutral stance, which points to real hesitation about the stock even amid the improving headline numbers. The portfolio's softer segments back up that hesitation. Business and Industry revenue declined 2.6% as ABM worked through the departure of a large client in the United Kingdom and continuing weakness in the Northern California commercial real estate market, where Salmirs said rival providers are pricing contracts at levels ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM) has chosen not to match. Aviation's operating margin fell to 5.6% from 6.8% as airline customers, under pressure from higher fuel expenses, pushed back on what they pay for service. Technical Solutions revenue grew just 4%, slowed by roughly $15 million in project delays after a major client opted to direct capital elsewhere for the time being. Manufacturing and distribution margin narrowed to 8.4% from 8.9% as ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM) absorbed both continued investment in its sales organization and additional amortization tied to the WGNSTAR deal. Interest expense also rose $4.2 million, driven by higher borrowings used to fund WGNSTAR and working-capital requirements. The businesses driving so much of the bullish narrative, semiconductor, microgrid, and data center work, still derive roughly 15% to 20% of their revenue from individual projects rather than contracts that repeat automatically. What The Smart Money Sees Harris Associates added to its position by 2% during the second quarter of 2026, ending the period with 2,912,307 shares worth $128.8 million, the largest hedge fund stake in the name. Pzena Investment Management increased its holding by 19% to 1,808,203 shares worth $80.0 million, and AQR Capital Management more than doubled its position, up 109%, to 768,980 shares worth $34.0 million. Total hedge fund ownership dropped to 21 funds from 28 the prior quarter, a decline that runs against the grain of the operational progress ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM) reported. Short interest stands at 5.45% of the float, a level consistent with a genuine, organized bearish position rather than incidental hedging, and shares changed hands at 11.11 times forward earnings as of September 18, 2026, a modest multiple that lines up with the three Hold and Neutral ratings still attached to the stock. Takeaway The three cautious analysts highlighted here who addressed ABM Industries Incorporated (NYSE:ABM)'s quarter raised their price targets, yet none moved to a rating that would count as a genuine endorsement, a pattern that captures where the stock sits today: improving on the metrics that matter most, cash generation, leverage, and exposure to semiconductor and data center spending, while still carrying real drag from a departed UK client, pressured aviation margins, and project-based revenue that hasn't yet become recurring. Truist's framing of a "light catalyst path" suggests the next re-rating, if it comes, will need Technical Solutions' expected fourth-quarter rebound and further progress converting the semiconductor pipeline into recurring business to actually show up in the numbers. While we acknowledge the potential of ABM as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.content: Better Energy Sector ETF: Vanguard's VDE Targeting Traditional Oil and Gas Giants vs. Invesco's Solar-Focused TAN Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool Tue, September 22, 2026 at 12:51 PM PDT 4 min read IVZ VDE ^GSPC The Vanguard Energy ETF (NYSEMKT:VDE) offers broad, low-cost exposure to traditional fossil fuel companies, while the Invesco Solar ETF (NYSEMKT:TAN) provides a high-conviction, specialized bet on the global solar power industry. Energy investing is not a monolith. While the Vanguard fund tracks a broad basket of traditional U.S. energy producers, the Invesco fund targets a specific, high-growth renewable niche. Comparing these two funds highlights the massive trade-offs between diversified fossil-fuel exposure and the high-volatility, thematic world of solar technology. The fund was launched in 2004. The Invesco Solar ETF maintains a tighter portfolio of 35 holdings, focusing on companies in the solar industry across energy (56%), utilities (31%), and industrials (5%). This concentration means the fund is sensitive to specific regulatory and technological shifts. Its largest positions include First Solar at 9.81%, Nextpower at 8.84%, and Enlight Renewable Energy at 8.19%. The fund was launched in 2008. These factors make energy ETFs an excellent way to efficiently invest in the industry. The Vanguard Energy ETF (VDE) and the Invesco Solar ETF (TAN) provide investors with very different approaches to doing so. Story Continues VDE has benefited from both the AI trend and the conflict in the Middle East, delivering a spectacular one-year return of nearly 50%. Combined with its low expense ratio, VDE is ideal for investors who want to hold for the long term. TAN is for those seeking to invest in the renewable energy sector, or who prefer not to contribute funds to traditional fossil fuel companies. In addition, the arrival of AI signals long-term growth potential for TAN, since many of the tech companies spending on AI prefer clean energy alternatives for electricity generation. articles.title: NY Fed's Perli says monetary policy toolkit working very well
articles.content: NY Fed's Perli says monetary policy toolkit working very well FILE PHOTO: View of the facade as construction continues on the Federal Reserve Board building, in Washington, D.C., U.S., September 17, 2025. REUTERS/Ken Cedeno/File Photo · Reuters By Michael S. Derby Tue, September 22, 2026 at 1:27 PM PDT 2 min read By Michael S. Derby NEW YORK, Sept 22 (Reuters) - The Federal Reserve's monetary policy control toolkit continues to be very effective, Roberto Perli, a New York Fed official ‌responsible for implementing short-term interest rate policy for the central bank, said on Tuesday. "We ‌have maintained very strong interest rate control, we have kept reserves within the ample range, and our Treasury bill purchases ​have run smoothly," Perli said. He is manager of the New York Fed's System Open Market Account. His comments came from closing remarks at an event held by the New York Fed on Treasury market issues. Perli leads the technical implementation of monetary policy to achieve the Fed's employment and inflation ‌mandates. He also said recent central bank ⁠actions to add liquidity to the financial system, which are currently paused, are not a preset course, suggesting the Fed could again buy Treasury bills ⁠if it thought it needed to bolster market liquidity. He also said so-called Reserve Management Purchases of Treasury bills will be adapted to market liquidity needs. When it comes to Treasury bill buying, "the recent decisions ​to set ​them at zero are no different in spirit than ​any of the other decisions the ‌Desk has made since RMPs started in December of last year," Perli said. The Fed had been buying bills in large quantities to bolster market liquidity levels and to ensure firm control over the federal funds target rate range, the institution's main tool to achieve its policy goals. It stopped buying recently after concluding the market had the needed amount of liquidity. The buying had been ‌technical in nature and was not designed to provide ​stimulus to the market, even as the purchases increased ​the overall size of the Fed's balance ​sheet. Perli said in his remarks that the New York Fed has a ‌handle on the factors that govern the RMPs. The ​New York Fed "process for ​forecasting reserves is robust and generally quite accurate," Perli said, adding "forecast misses over the past four years represent a very small fraction of total reserves supply and are easily ​accommodated by our ample reserves framework." Perli ‌also said in his remarks that "strictly from a monetary policy implementation perspective, offering ​a centrally cleared version of our standing repo operations would offer some clear benefits." (Reporting ​by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Edmund Klamann) Terms and Privacy Policy Your Privacy Choices CA Privacy Notice More Info

articles.title: Comfort Shoe Parent to Trotters and Softwalk Set to Cease Operations
articles.content: Comfort Shoe Parent to Trotters and Softwalk Set to Cease Operations Footwear News · Courtesy of Phoenix Footwear Group Vicki M. Young Tue, September 22, 2026 at 12:47 PM PDT 2 min read PXFG Phoenix Footwear Group is set to cease operations over the next 60 days. That's the latest update for the parent of the Softwalk and Trotters comfort shoe brands, according to a post by Allison Hannon on LinkedIn. Phoenix also owns Bueno Footwear, which it acquired in 2017. The 144-year-old Carlsbad, Calif.-based firm is also the U.S. distributor for the Los Cabos and Eos shoe brands. More from WWD Annamaria Brivio Is Taking Her Biggest Step Yet Sneex, Clarks, Alo and More Shoe Releases You Might Have Missed This Week The Best Sneakers for Supination to Buy Online Now The company began operations under the name Daniel Green Company, known for its slippers and comfort footwear. In 1999, it shut down a manufacturing plan in Upstate New York and began outsourcing production. In 2000, it acquired Penobscot Shoe company, which owned the Trotters and Softwalk brands. Penobscott was founded in 1935 under the name Philco Shoe Co. The company has long had a foothold in the Maine community through its Penobscott acquisition where a facility handles warehousing and distribution. The Daniel Green brand was sold to Elan-Polo Inc. in 2001, and the Daniel Green Company was renamed Phoenix Footwear Group in 2002 after it was reincorporated following the sale of the Daniel Green brand. Shoe production for Trotters and Softwalk is primarily produced in Brazil, according to a Securities and Exchange Commission filing in 2004. Shares of Phoenix Footwear, which once traded on the New York Stock Exchange, moved to over-the-counter trading in 2011 due to its small market capitalization. The shares moved to the Pink OTC Market in 2025, which is the highly speculative tier in the OTC Markets. Also known as the Pink Sheets, this tier includes distressed stocks that do not need to provide ongoing financial reporting. There has been an increased focus on comfort footwear, such as for work boots, and even for cushioned road-running sneakers t o orthopedic mary janes. But even with that focus, there's no indication for what the future will be for the Softwalk, Trotters, and Bueno brands. A visit to the Trotters.com site said "We are temporarily pausing Trotters.com," noting that the notice "isn't goodbye. It's simply a pause in the online journey." The Softwalk website posted a similar message. Over at the Bueno website, where the shoes are handmade in Turkey, it also noted that it was suspending online sales, but did not state that the suspension was a pause. "Thank you for being part of our journey," the site said, indicating that the shutdown might be the end of the road for Bueno Footwear. articles.title: Ennis (EBF) Grows Sales but Earns Less. Are Legal Items Hiding a Better Business?
articles.content: Ennis (EBF) Grows Sales but Earns Less. Are Legal Items Hiding a Better Business? Jeff Lewis Tue, September 22, 2026 at 9:52 PM EDT 3 min read EBF Ennis, Inc. (NYSE: EBF ) reported higher sales and lower earnings for the quarter ended August 31, 2026, but legal items complicate the comparison. The underlying business held up better than the headline profit decline suggests, while paper costs created genuine margin pressure. The September 21 release showed revenue of $102 million, up 3.3% from $98.7 million. Net earnings fell to $9.4 million from $13.2 million. Investors need to distinguish the litigation effects from changes in demand, acquisition contributions, and production costs. Bull Case The prior-year quarter included a $5.3 million favorable litigation judgment, while the current quarter included an unrelated $700,000 litigation charge. Management said diluted earnings per share increased $0.02 after excluding these items from both periods. This non-GAAP comparison removes the specified litigation effects from reported diluted earnings per share. That modest improvement is more encouraging than the reported earnings decline. Gross profit also increased to $30.5 million from $30.1 million, showing that the larger revenue base produced additional gross profit despite a lower margin. Ennis, Inc. (NYSE:EBF) generated $34.1 million of operating cash flow in the first half, compared with $18.4 million a year earlier. Cash reached $54 million as of August 31, and management reported no debt. That financial position provides room to support operations and acquisitions without immediate refinancing pressure. Supply continuity is another positive. Ennis, Inc. (NYSE:EBF) has received shipments from alternative carbonless-paper suppliers following the closure of the sole domestic producer. Management continues to expect uninterrupted product availability and customer service. Maintaining supply protects the ability to fulfill orders while the business adapts to higher input costs. Bear Case Acquisitions contributed approximately $2.3 million of the $3.3 million quarterly revenue increase. Subtracting the disclosed acquisition contribution leaves roughly $1 million of additional sales, or about 1% of prior-year revenue, based on rounded figures. The reported growth rate therefore overstates the improvement outside those acquisition contributions. Gross margin declined to 29.9% from 30.5%, a decrease of 60 basis points. Management attributed the decline primarily to higher carbonless-paper costs recognized in cost of sales. That pressure affects the economics of producing and selling printed products independently of the litigation comparison. Story Continues Ennis, Inc. (NYSE:EBF) needs pricing, product mix, or productivity improvements to offset those costs. Reliable access to paper addresses availability, while purchasing terms and selling prices determine how much profit remains on each order. Cash generation also requires context. Inventory declined during the quarter after the earlier buildup to protect supply. Investors should assess whether operating cash flow remains strong once inventory levels stabilize, since working-capital movements can change cash generation without equivalent changes in earnings. Hedge Fund Sentiment The filings available so far reflect positions held before Ennis, Inc. (NYSE:EBF) reported its quarterly results. Insider Monkey's database showed 15 hedge funds holding Ennis, Inc. (NYSE:EBF) at the end of 2Q2026, up from 14 funds three months earlier. Conclusion Ennis, Inc. (NYSE:EBF) looks more resilient after accounting for the litigation items, supported by strong first-half cash generation and a debt-free balance sheet. However, acquisition contributions explain most of the quarterly sales increase, and paper costs are squeezing margins. Growth outside acquisitions, gross-margin stabilization, and cash flow after inventory normalization will determine whether the business is improving sustainably. While we acknowledge the potential of EBF as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: Strive CEO: Bitcoin Could ‘Go to Infinity' as Dollar Debt Crisis Breaks
articles.content: Strive CEO: Bitcoin Could ‘Go to Infinity' as Dollar Debt Crisis Breaks Darryn Pollock Tue, September 22, 2026 at 9:51 PM EDT 2 min read BTC-USD ASST DX-Y.NYB Strive CEO Matt Cole says Bitcoin (BTC) could effectively go to infinity against the US dollar, arguing that a mounting Washington debt crisis, not Bitcoin's own scarcity, is what will ultimately break the currency's value. Cole made the comments on Bloomberg Crypto, as digital assets have reclaimed $3 trillion in market value since January. Strive, a Bitcoin treasury company that raises capital to buy and hold BTC on its balance sheet, has been one of the more aggressive buyers through the cycle. A Debt Crisis, Not a Bitcoin Story Cole argued that the 10-year Treasury yield would already sit north of 10% if the Federal Reserve and the Treasury Department stepped back from the bond market entirely. He credits Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent with capping long-end rates for now, but says that intervention only delays a reckoning, since neither party in Washington shows any willingness to cut spending. "We think Bitcoin can effectively go to infinity versus the dollar." — Matt Cole, on Bloomberg https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NFQVh9AH0lM That logic underpins Strive's public forecast of a 50% compound annual growth rate for Bitcoin through 2030, a figure Cole calls conservative given the asset's past bull-market cycles, a view he first laid out when he called the bear market over last month. It also explains why Strive's SATA preferred stock, which pays a daily cash dividend, has, according to Cole, outperformed Bitcoin itself by more than 100% in 2026 even as BTC has traded roughly flat. Why the Treasury Model Persists Cole also pushed back on the idea that the Bitcoin treasury company model is fading. He argues it never broke, only that firms without a clear thesis or sound debt terms struggled once the bear market hit, while disciplined buyers kept accumulating even as Wall Street treasuries resumed buying. Cole's framing puts Bitcoin's price action second to a wager on US fiscal dysfunction, one that only pays off if bond markets and the dollar move the way he expects over the next several years. articles.title: Westinghouse Air Brake (WAB) Signs $700 Million-Plus Rail Services Deal. Can Profits Grow?
articles.content: Westinghouse Air Brake (WAB) Signs $700 Million-Plus Rail Services Deal. Can Profits Grow? Jeff Lewis Tue, September 22, 2026 at 9:43 PM EDT 3 min read WAB Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation (NYSE: WAB ) announced on September 21 a services agreement worth more than $700 million with La Compagnie du TransGuinéen. Combined with locomotive orders placed in 2024, announced agreements for the Simandou project now exceed $1.2 billion. The railway stretches more than 600 kilometers between the Simandou mine and Guinea's Port of Morebaya. The new agreement extends the relationship beyond locomotive delivery into ongoing fleet support. For investors, the opportunity is to earn revenue throughout the equipment's operating life. Is Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation (WAB) The Best Railroad Stock To Buy Now? BULL CASE Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation (NYSE:WAB) will provide scheduled and unscheduled maintenance, parts, component overhauls, logistics support, remote diagnostics, and training. These activities create multiple opportunities to serve the same fleet after the initial equipment sale. That is an attractive business model when maintenance needs translate into repeat orders and efficient service delivery. Familiarity with the locomotives should help technicians diagnose problems and plan repairs. Remote monitoring could also help identify faults before they cause prolonged downtime, strengthening the customer's incentive to maintain the relationship. Local workforce development and partnerships with Guinean businesses could improve responsiveness as the operation matures. Over time, an experienced local team could reduce dependence on specialists traveling to the site and make parts planning more efficient. The broader freight business provides a profitable base. Second-quarter freight revenue increased 16.9% to $2.24 billion, while its GAAP operating margin rose to 22.5% from 21.6%. Those results demonstrate existing earnings capacity, although the new agreement's contribution will depend on its own pricing and execution costs. BEAR CASE Westinghouse Air Brake Technologies Corporation (NYSE:WAB) has announced a multiyear contract value, not $700 million of annual revenue or immediate cash receipts. The combined $1.2 billion also includes earlier equipment orders. Treating the entire amount as new business from this announcement would overstate the incremental opportunity. The release does not specify the exact contract duration, revenue commencement date, annual revenue schedule, or expected service margin. Those details matter because the same headline value can produce very different returns depending on how quickly work is performed, costs are incurred, and customers pay. Story Continues Recurring service opportunities also do not guarantee smooth quarterly growth. Second-quarter freight-services sales declined 4.2%, reflecting lower modernization deliveries, as expected. articles.title: May Mobility's SPAC Merger: Is This a Road to Nowhere for Investors?
articles.content: May Mobility's SPAC Merger: Is This a Road to Nowhere for Investors? Daniel Miller, The Motley Fool Tue, September 22, 2026 at 9:50 PM EDT 6 min read ACGC NVDA Investors eager to buy into the futuristic vision of profitable driverless vehicles will get their chance soon . May Mobility is aiming to become the first U.S. publicly listed pure-play option for an autonomous ride-hailing technology company. It is poised to go public through a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC), merging with ACP Holdings Acquisition (NASDAQ: ACGC) that values the combined company at roughly $1.4 billion. It's expected to operate as May Mobility. trading on the Nasdaq exchange under MAY. But before investors get too excited, let's pump the brakes and take a look at the details. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » Opportunity knocks It's easy for investors to get excited about the opportunity, but many might not be aware of the potential market size or growth prospects. The global robotaxi market is projected to reach about $415 billion by 2035, with the U.S. accounting for a roughly $48 billion slice of that pie. The fleet of U.S. commercial autonomous vehicles (AVs) is projected to expand from only about 4,000 vehicles currently to around 35,000 by 2030 -- or about 8% of the ride-sharing market. A year ago this month, Bank of America projected that the long-term U.S. total addressable market (TAM) for AV ride-hailing is a trillion-dollar opportunity as companies such as May Mobility aim to replace the drivers that take roughly 70% of every fare. It's also important for investors to realize how early in the game this is: Alphabet 's Waymo, with an estimated $350 million in annualized revenue, would represent only about 0.5% of U.S. ride-hailing bookings. The opportunity is potentially lucrative, albeit still very early in the game. So, what makes May Mobility intriguing? An asset-light transition May Mobility is moving to an asset-light model. At the company's initial U.S. ride-hailing launch site, it estimates the costs for the safety driver; vehicles (financing, depreciation, insurance, maintenance); site operations (fuel/charging, depot operations, and staff); and remote vehicle supervisors, software maintenance, and field engineers. In this asset-heavy scenario, May Mobility's projections put its annual revenue per vehicle between $130,000 to $150,000, as it keeps all the revenue. But because it also incurs all the costs, it checks in with a negative gross margin per vehicle with a safety driver. Story Continues Under its asset-light model, which includes removing the safety driver, May Mobility transfers the vehicle costs as well as the site operating costs to a fleet operating partner, although it will still incur the costs for remote supervisors, field engineers, and software maintenance. This scenario would come with a larger fleet size thanks to a fleet-operator partner, and lower revenue ($50,000 to $72,000 per vehicle) as it splits the sales with that partner. But it checks in with a gross margin per vehicle between $35,000 to $50,000 annually because it would push off significant costs and could scale up more quickly without needing to purchase and own the fleet. There's further upside with management targeting a 50% reduction in its bill of materials (BOM) by the end of 2028. That's from cost savings realized through computing and sensors with next-generation chip alternatives and as lidar/radar/camera markets scale up and mature. May Mobility also expects to reduce its BOM through cost reductions in hardware components and integration when its software could be installed by the original equipment manufacturer (with Toyota as a partner for AV-ready vehicle platforms at scale) rather than installing it in vehicles afterwards. Over the long term without drivers, management is targeting gross margins of about 70%, and margins under earnings before interest and taxes around 30%. How going public helps When the SPAC deal and merger closes, it could provide May Mobility with up to $337 million in funding. Investors can look at the economics and do the math: In 2025, the company generated roughly $10 million in revenue with a 27% gross margin, while burning $93 million in cash. The SPAC funds should enable it to strengthen its balance sheet and liquidity, finance added research and development, invest in the supply chain to reduce costs, and launch new in markets without drivers. However, without a major cash pile, the cash burn could erode its liquidity rather quickly. What it all means It's an exciting time in an automotive industry that's poised to evolve rapidly over the next decade. However, investors must understand that this is an exceptionally high-risk investment currently. May Mobility's 27% gross margin is an encouraging beginning, but the cash burn is significant and will only increase in the near term. It will rely heavily on the $337 million of fresh capital from its public debut, and that could erode rapidly. Investors also have to consider that despite being in the early innings, there are some heavyweights accelerating forward, including market leader Waymo and Tesla 's slow but steady progress with its Cybercab business. Tesla's Cybercab. Image source: Tesla. May Mobility is intriguing, but this only scratches the surface. Potential shareholders must read through the investor presentation, available here , and recognize that this could end in a total loss. For now, this should be a company that most retail investors watch curiously from the sidelines, especially as this debut tests investor demand for a pure-play AV ride-hailing company. More domestic manufacturing incentives and customer interest in secure supply support that plan. A successful SK Hynix move could eventually erode part of Micron's U.S.-supply differentiation. Memory manufacturing is becoming strategic enough that SK Hynix is considering putting advanced capacity on American soil, and Intel's delayed Ohio project suddenly gives it a potentially valuable asset to negotiate with. Photo from Intel Corp website The most useful strategic comparison is Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: AMD ), which bought FPGA leader Xilinx in 2022 and integrated programmable silicon into a much broader data-center portfolio. The IPO could put a price on an asset Intel partially kept Intel bought Altera for $16.7 billion in 2015 before separating the business and selling control to Silver Lake. An IPO would create a new market valuation for Intel Corporation's (NASDAQ:INTC) remaining interest. That matters because Intel needs capital. A strong Altera valuation could therefore crystallize value in an asset investors currently bury inside Intel's much larger turnaround. The downside is that IPO appetite for anything carrying an AI label can run ahead of operating reality. Altera makes programmable chips across industrial, communications, aerospace and data-center markets. Management has projected mid-20% revenue growth in 2026, but investors will still have to determine how much of that growth is genuinely AI-driven. Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ:AMD) shows what Altera ultimately has to compete against. Xilinx gave AMD FPGAs, adaptive SoCs and software that can sit beside its EPYC CPUs and Instinct accelerators. That bundle can be attractive in heterogeneous systems. The bear case is that AMD paid heavily to assemble that portfolio, and integrating multiple product families does not guarantee every FPGA workload migrates into AMD's ecosystem. Funds became much more interested in both chipmakers Insider Monkey counted 138 hedge funds holding Intel in Q2, up from 112 in Q1. AQR Capital Management held about 10.7 million shares after trimming its stake roughly 7%. AMD ownership jumped to 164 funds from 134, while Marshall Wace held about 3.9 million shares after a modest increase. Intel had approximately 152.2 million shares sold short on August 31, about 3% of public float. Story Continues Altera's offering terms have not been set, so $2 billion remains a reported fundraising possibility rather than a finalized deal. What the IPO could do is make a hidden part of Intel easier to value while giving investors a fresh public benchmark against AMD's Xilinx strategy. While we acknowledge the potential of INTC and AMD as investments, we believe certain other AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.content: Why AutoZone Stock Rallied Today Joe Tenebruso, The Motley Fool Tue, September 22, 2026 at 10:00 PM EDT 2 min read AZO NVDA Shares of AutoZone (NYSE: AZO) rose on Tuesday after the automotive replacement parts and accessories distributor reported stronger-than-expected profits. Image source: Getty Images. Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 15x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue » AutoZone is expanding its store count at a solid clip AutoZone's net sales grew 5.6% year over year to $6.6 billion in its fiscal 2026 fourth quarter, which ended on Aug. 29. The auto-parts purveyor opened 175 stores during the quarter and a total of 374 over the trailing 12 months. AutoZone ended the period with 8,031 stores, including 6,863 stores in the U.S., 1,001 in Mexico, and 167 in Brazil. Additionally, same-store sales, which measure revenue from locations open for at least a year, increased by 2.7%, or 1.5% when excluding foreign currency fluctuations. "We grew our total store count, opening the most stores ever in a single year, improved on our assortment and in-stock positions, and continued to invest in systems to deliver even better customer service," CEO Phil Daniele said during a conference call with analysts. Better still, tariff refunds helped to drive AutoZone's operating profit up by 10% to $1.3 billion. Its net income, in turn, increased 11% to $931.6 million. And its earnings per share, boosted by stock buybacks, jumped 15% to $56.05. That topped Wall Street's estimates, which had called for per-share profits of $53.89, according to Yahoo! Finance. Management sees further growth in the U.S. and internationally Despite higher gas prices and a challenging overall economic environment, AutoZone expects more gains in the year ahead. "Over the last eight weeks of the quarter, our sales results strengthened, and we feel we are well-positioned for sales growth in fiscal 2027," Daniele said. articles.title: Why Bernstein Still Sees 46% Upside in Zscaler (ZS) but Downgraded Palo Alto (PANW)
articles.content: Why Bernstein Still Sees 46% Upside in Zscaler (ZS) but Downgraded Palo Alto (PANW) Habib Ur Rehman Wed, September 23, 2026 at 12:13 AM EDT 3 min read ZS PANW Wall Street has spent much of 2026 rewarding cybersecurity stocks for the risks created by AI. Bernstein now thinks the easy part of that trade is over, with one major exception. Bernstein analyst Peter Weed raised his target on Zscaler, Inc. (NASDAQ: ZS ) to $298 and maintained an Outperform rating on September 17. The target implied roughly 46% upside when the call was published. At the same time, Bernstein downgraded Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ: PANW ) and several other cyber names to Market Perform. The distinction is valuation rather than a belief that AI security demand disappears. Bernstein Says Zscaler Is the Only Cyber Stock With Big Upside Left. Palo Alto Just Got Downgraded Zscaler has to prove its underperformance created an opportunity Zscaler entered the analyst call down about 11.5% in 2026 while many peers had rallied. Bernstein argued that its shift from opportunity-based selling toward deeper customer relationships is beginning to work. Zscaler reported a 115% dollar-based net retention rate in fiscal Q1, and management later said that level had remained fairly stable for several quarters. For Zscaler, Inc. (NASDAQ:ZS), that creates a straightforward rerating case. If existing customers adopt more products while AI increases the number of users, agents and workloads requiring security, growth can remain strong without the stock carrying the same expectations as hotter peers. There is a reason the discount exists. Zscaler still faces slower incremental ARR growth and aggressive competition from companies bundling multiple security functions. If large enterprises prefer consolidation, a focused zero-trust specialist must keep proving it deserves separate budget. Palo Alto Networks, Inc. (NASDAQ:PANW) has almost the opposite problem. Its broad platform gives enterprises a single vendor across network, cloud and security operations, and acquisitions have expanded that reach. Bernstein's downgrade reflects the price investors are already paying for that strength. Integration costs, a larger share count and slowing growth comparisons raise the hurdle. Fund positioning does not show investors abandoning either name Insider Monkey tracked 52 hedge funds holding Zscaler in Q2, up from 46 in Q1. Palo Alto ownership edged up to 89 funds from 87. Fisher Asset Management increased its PANW position 2,143% to about 5.8 million shares. Zscaler's August 31 short-interest snapshot was about 6.35 million shares, roughly 4.7% of public float and 2.9 days to cover. Bernstein's call is interesting because it is not simply bullish cybersecurity commentary. It draws a line inside an already popular trade. Palo Alto may remain the stronger platform business, but Zscaler now has something PANW increasingly lacks: a valuation setup where Wall Street can still imagine a large rerating. articles.title: “The New Clippy”: Benioff Uses Salesforce’s Biggest Product Launch in Years to Challenge Microsoft
articles.content: “The New Clippy”: Benioff Uses Salesforce’s Biggest Product Launch in Years to Challenge Microsoft Sheryar Siddiq Wed, September 23, 2026 at 12:46 AM EDT 4 min read CRM MSFT Marc Benioff is never one to pass up a chance to take a jab at Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ: MSFT ), and Dreamforce 2026 was no different. The Salesforce CEO used the company's flagship annual conference in San Francisco to announce AIforce, the biggest product launch Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE: CRM ) has made in years, and to once again refer to Microsoft's Copilot as "the new Clippy," doubling down on a dig he made two years ago. What AIforce Actually Does Salesforce is positioning AIforce as an open, provider-agnostic layer rather than a single proprietary assistant. It's intended to work across multiple AI systems, including Anthropic's Claude, via a specific integration called Claudeforce, which Salesforce claims guarantees zero data retention by the model provider, as well as ChatGPT, Slack, and other environments. Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) made the announcement alongside an additional strategic marker: a fiscal 2030 revenue target of $63 billion, which management reiterated at Dreamforce. A Rivalry That Goes Back To 2024 Benioff portrayed AIforce as the solution to what he calls the "Fantasyland" problem, arguing that competing AI solutions, including Copilot, lack the dependable, controlled business-data layer required to consistently run enterprise operations. It's a continuation of a public feud that's been going on since at least Dreamforce 2024, when Benioff first compared Copilot to Clippy, Microsoft's widely mocked, uninvited desktop assistant from the late 1990s, saying, "We all know now that Microsoft Copilot is basically the new Microsoft Clippy, that customers have not gotten value from it." He's returned to that theme several times since, including at Davos, in an October 2024 written critique saying that Microsoft "lacks the data, metadata, and enterprise security models to create real corporate intelligence," and on a podcast where he labeled Copilot a "tremendous disservice" to the AI sector. Favorable Analyst Response Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) shares closed at $255.65 on September 15, after a nearly 34% rally in the previous month following a rough start to 2026 that saw the stock tumble as much as 37%. That momentum was fueled by Salesforce's most recent quarterly results, which featured $11.35 billion in revenue, exceeding Wall Street's projections on both the top and bottom lines. Analyst reaction to the Dreamforce announcements was also favorable, with Stifel raising its price target for Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) to $300 from $275 while reaffirming a Buy rating, citing six distinct revenue channels laid out by the company for monetizing its new AI stack, including additional core licenses, premium SKU upgrades, Agentforce spending, Data 360, Agent Fabric and Guardian, and APIs, MCPs and related infrastructure. Story Continues Institutional Positioning Institutional posture shifted in similar directions for the two competitors. Salesforce, Inc. (NYSE:CRM) saw hedge fund ownership fall slightly, from 101 in the first quarter to 99 in the second. Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) experienced a greater fall, from 282 funds to 273, though both declines predate the Dreamforce event and are more likely to reflect broader software-sector positioning moves than a direct read on this contest. How AIforce Takes On Copilot Salesforce's pitch for AIforce as an open layer that brings Salesforce data, permissions and business logic into Claude, ChatGPT and other AI interfaces could still be an important competitive distinction, particularly for companies that want to use Salesforce context across multiple AI environments. The emphasis on regulated data access and zero data retention in Claudeforce directly addresses enterprise trust problems, which have hampered AI adoption elsewhere. Conference Hype, Unclear Pricing, and Microsoft's Distribution Juggernaut However, Salesforce's stock has a documented history of rallying on analyst upgrades and conference announcements before reversing those gains, as seen with earlier JPMorgan and Citi buy calls in 2026, and pricing and adoption uncertainty around Agentforce remain unanswered questions even as new products pile on top of it. Microsoft's competition is also far from theoretical, considering Copilot's distribution advantage via Office and Dynamics 365. Insider Monkey's Bottom Line Investors should keep an eye on whether this round of enthusiasm lasts longer than previous Dreamforce-fueled surges, with confirmation likely to come from the next quarterly report, which will show whether Agentforce and now AIforce adoption numbers are translating into the kind of Data and AI revenue growth analysts are projecting with their newly set $300 price targets. Given the remaining uncertainty around how quickly Salesforce can convert AI adoption into meaningful revenue, the more reliable signal for investors will be concrete adoption and revenue-conversion data in upcoming earnings, rather than the announcement itself or the pre-Dreamforce rally that followed Salesforce's latest earnings report. While we acknowledge the potential of CRM as an investment, we believe certain AI stocks offer greater upside potential and carry less downside risk. articles.title: Nike (NKE): Wall Street Tests Whether the Turnaround Can Outrun Weak Demand Ahead of Q1 Results
articles.content: Nike (NKE): Wall Street Tests Whether the Turnaround Can Outrun Weak Demand Ahead of Q1 Results Faheem Tahir Wed, September 23, 2026 at 12:07 AM EDT 5 min read NKE NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE) heads into its October 1 fiscal 2027 first-quarter report with Wall Street focused less on whether revenue can beat a modest guide and more on whether improving margins and performance categories can offset weak demand in the lifestyle business. The latest warning comes from Stifel, which cut its price target to $40 from $45 on September 21 while keeping a Hold rating. The firm expects a more promotional Western marketplace and a tougher fiscal fourth-quarter gross-margin comparison, cutting its FY2027 and FY2028 adjusted EPS estimates by $0.20 each, to $1.70 and $2.05. Nike (NKE): Wall Street Tests Whether the Turnaround Can Outrun Weak Demand Ahead of Q1 Results Mbuso Sydwell Nkosi/Shutterstock.com The Bull Case: Sport, Wholesale and the World Cup Can Buy Nike Time There are still tangible signs that NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE)'s reset is working in parts of the portfolio. Performance grew mid-single digits in fiscal 2026, while Running posted five consecutive quarters of double-digit growth and added roughly $1 billion in revenue. North American wholesale revenue grew 10% in the fourth quarter, and management said the business benefited from lower returns, cancellations and discounts rather than simply pushing more inventory into stores. The World Cup provides another near-term tailwind. Stifel estimates the tournament could add about $300 million to Q1 revenue, while NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE) has already pointed to stronger football demand and said its World Cup product launches were gaining traction. Stifel also continues to expect revenue above consensus, noting that Nike has exceeded its own revenue guidance for seven consecutive quarters. Margin improvement could provide another offset. NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE)'s Q4 gross margin, excluding the $986 million tariff-recovery benefit, was down just 10 basis points year-over-year, better than its guidance. Management attributed the improvement partly to lower discounts, cancellations and sales-related reserves and expects supply-chain restructuring to support margins in FY2027. The Bear Case: The New Product Pipeline Still Has to Prove Itself The problem is that NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE)'s strongest performance categories are not yet large enough to erase weakness elsewhere. Sportswear declined double digits in Q4, while management expects Sportswear and Jordan streetwear to remain negative through FY2027, even with improvement in the second half. Together, those businesses represent roughly half of revenue. That is where Stifel's latest update becomes important. The firm sees insufficient consumer demand for Nike's new products and continued contraction in Hoops Classics, which represents about 18% of revenue. UBS has also pointed to deteriorating global sales trends and expects a Q1 EPS miss, while Citi sees elevated promotions and difficult North American comparisons weighing on Q2. Baird similarly cited weaker marketplace conditions, more negative retailer commentary on athletic lifestyle sales and pressure from Nike's China e-commerce reset. Story Continues China remains another unresolved drag. Greater China revenue fell 17% in Q4, and management expects near-term trends to remain broadly consistent with that decline. Although full-price realization and sell-through have improved in some areas, NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE) is still cleaning up inventory and reducing supply into the market. Valuation Premium Faces Growing Skepticism Nike's valuation and positioning add another layer to that debate. The stock traded at a 20.66 forward P/E as of September 21, compared with 10.46 for Deckers Outdoor, 14.27 for On Holding and 11.47 for Adidas. Hedge fund ownership also fell to 56 funds in the second quarter from 71 in the first, although several individual managers increased their stakes sharply. Arrowstreet Capital raised its position 10,175% to 5.62 million shares, while Renaissance Technologies increased its stake 1,192% to 4.07 million shares. Meanwhile, short interest climbed to 75.59 million shares as of August 31 from 57.37 million a month earlier, putting short interest at 7.92% of the float and 5.10% of shares outstanding. The combination leaves NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE) with a higher valuation than several peers alongside reduced hedge fund participation and rising short interest, making evidence of a broader recovery increasingly important. The Takeaway: Q1 Is About the Quality of the Recovery The October 1 report therefore faces a higher bar than the headline revenue number suggests. A World Cup boost can support sales, but Wall Street is looking for evidence that demand is broadening beyond Running and football, particularly in Sportswear and Jordan, while gross-margin improvement survives a more promotional marketplace. That tension explains the recent estimate cuts despite some analysts retaining relatively constructive revenue expectations. UBS expects a Q1 EPS shortfall (five cents) and sees risk of a broader FY2027 reset at the November Investor Day, while BMO expects NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE) to reset its FY2027 outlook when it reports. For NIKE, Inc. (NYSE:NKE), the key question heading into October 1 is whether the turnaround is beginning to create healthier full-price demand, or merely shifting the mix toward the parts of the portfolio that are already working. The answer will also shape expectations heading into the November 16-17 Investor Day, where management is scheduled to outline the next phase of its growth strategy. articles.title: Trump and Xi begin high-stakes summit in Washington
articles.content: US President Donald Trump, right, greets Xi Jinping after the Chinese president’s plane landed at a military base near Washington last night © Getty Images Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on x (opens in a new window) Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on facebook (opens in a new window) Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on linkedin (opens in a new window) Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on whatsapp (opens in a new window) Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on x (opens in a new window) Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on facebook (opens in a new window) Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on linkedin (opens in a new window) Donald Trump and Xi Jinping extend trade truce to January on whatsapp (opens in a new window) Myles McCormick in Washington Published September 24 2026 Jump to comments section Print this page This is an on-site version of the White House Watch newsletter. You can read the previous edition here . Sign up for free here to get it on Tuesdays and Thursdays. Email us at [email protected] Hello from Washington and welcome to White House Watch. On our agenda today: Trump and Xi meet in Washington for pivotal summit Influencer Hasan Piker says Republican efforts to vilify him are falling short Republicans are splashing out on midterm election advertising All eyes are on Washington today, where Xi Jinping has arrived for a high-stakes two-day summit with Donald Trump (Follow along with the FT’s live blog here ). It is the Chinese president’s first visit to the US capital in more than a decade. And as my colleagues Demetri Sevastopulo and Joe Leahy report , it will involve plenty of fanfare. At the top of the agenda are trade relations and the creation of an AI dialogue to discuss risks posed by the technology. Shortly after Xi landed last night, US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent said the countries had agreed to extend their one-year trade truce, which was set to expire on November 10, until January 10. Xi is also expected to raise the subject of Taiwan. Trump sparked alarm in May when he said American arms sales to Taiwan were a “good negotiating chip” , suggesting that he might curtail US support for Taipei. But there will also be plenty of pomp and cultural events. A formal welcome ceremony will be held on the South Lawn of the White House this morning, featuring a military review and flyover by fighter jets and bombers. Trump and Xi walk side by side during the arrival ceremony. The Chinese president later said the two countries should be ‘partners, not rivals’ © Getty Images In the evening, the pair will be joined by their wives and a host of Big Tech and Wall Street executives for an official state dinner. On the guest list are Tesla boss Elon Musk, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman, Jane Fraser from Citigroup and Apple’s former chief Tim Cook. In a statement issued after his arrival last night, Xi said it was a “great pleasure” to pay a state visit to the US. The two countries should be “partners, not rivals”, the Chinese leader said, adding that 2026 was a “pivotal” year for US-China relations. Trump’s show of respect for his Chinese counterpart underlines the shift from his aggressive stance towards Beijing during his first term — an approach that has frustrated the ambitions of the hawks in his administration . But the US president’s changeable nature and willingness to deploy tariffs as a geopolitical weapon mean nothing is certain in the relationship. Amid all the fanfare of the next two days, the world will be watching attentively. Could you be the FT’s next stock picking champion? The FT’s new Stock Picking Game is a fast, fun way to test your trading instincts, sharpen your market expertise and compete for the chance to win £1,000. Terms and conditions apply. Register for season two now. The latest headlines Republicans are far outspending Democrats on advertising ahead of November 3’s midterm elections, reserving roughly $1bn in advertising slots between September 1 and election day, according to an FT analysis. A federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to temporarily restore White House access to CNN, MS Now and Politico after the news outlets had been banned by the president. A global bond rout has deepened as oil jumped back above $105 a barrel on Thursday, adding to inflation fears after the US Treasury market suffered its biggest fall since last year’s trade war sell-off. The US oil industry also warned there was no “silver bullet” solution to the supply crunch. Belgium’s foreign ministry has warned internally that the US under Trump is no longer a reliable ally , according to a document seen by the FT. The UK is reviewing its plan to transfer sovereignty of the Chagos Islands to Mauritius, after Trump renewed his opposition to the deal in a meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham. What we’re hearing Leftwing influencer Hasan Piker was accused by House Speaker Mike Johnson this month of wanting to lead the US down a “dark, dangerous, deadly road to communism”. But the prolific Twitch streamer — seen by many on the right as one of the most dangerous men in the country — told my colleague Guy Chazan that Republicans’ campaign of vilification “isn’t working”. “If you talk to me you very quickly realise I’m a fairly pragmatic person,” he told the FT, adding that the Financial Times was his “favourite newspaper”. Hasan Piker speaks at a Democratic campaign event in Michigan in April © Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Piker is a self-declared “socialist anti-imperialist” who once said America “deserved 9/11” (for which he later apologised) and has enraged supporters of Israel by saying that he would “vote for Hamas over Israel every time”. He was also banned in June from entering the UK because his presence “may not be conducive to the public good”. In an interview with the FT, the bogeyman of the Republican Party hit back at attempts to brand him a “dangerous, radical, Islamist, jihadist terrorist”. “A lot of these manosphere guys don’t know what they’re talking about — their level of involvement with politics is super, super basic,” Piker said. Viewpoints Donald Trump’s proposed diesel export ban will backfire , according to Lex’s Camilla Palladino. Martin Wolf says the Federal Reserve’s decision to raise interest rates in spite of Trump’s demands was “sensible” and “overdue” . Calling for closer EU-Canada ties without pooling sovereignty is an abdication of European responsibility , argues Martin Sandbu. As Germany’s Friedrich Merz comes under pressure and speculation grows over who could succeed him at the helm of Europe’s biggest economy, Janan Ganesh maintains the west does not have a leadership problem . While existential fears over technology rise, the FT editorial board says the US and China can work together on AI security . articles.title: Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth
articles.content: Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on x (opens in a new window) Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on facebook (opens in a new window) Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on linkedin (opens in a new window) Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on whatsapp (opens in a new window) Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on x (opens in a new window) Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on facebook (opens in a new window) Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on linkedin (opens in a new window) Fitzcarraldo – inside the chicest publisher on earth on whatsapp (opens in a new window) Helen Bain . Photography by Wendy Huynh Published September 25 2026 Jump to comments section Print this page Unlock the Editor’s Digest for free Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter. At the age of 29, Jacques Testard set up a publishing house because no one in publishing would employ him. Born in France and schooled in London, he had wanted to go into academia before a series of internships made him realise that publishing was “another way to be serious about books”. In 2014, when he struggled to find a permanent opening, he decided to launch his own house. His ambition was not just to be an editor but to find and publish “writers at the cutting edge of contemporary literature” – including, significantly, work in translation. He had 18 months until the money ran out. “I thought, ‘I’ll give this a go and see what happens, and maybe in a few years’ time someone will give me a job.’” Every publisher is a story, says Ray O’Meara, the house’s art director, and the story of Fitzcarraldo Editions is very simple. Twelve years ago, mainstream UK publishers did not believe there was a market for translated literature. It was a gap Testard was able to plug. The first book he published that year was Zone by Mathias Énard, a 521-page stream-of-consciousness account of an amphetamine-fuelled journey across Italy, written in a single sentence, which he had discovered when he read it in French. For the new house, it was something of a mission statement. That same year, still the sole employee, Testard made an offer for Svetlana Alexievich’s oral history Second-hand Time . The book was already a bestseller in Russia and had sold well in France and Germany but there was no competition for the UK rights. Testard’s opening bid of $2,000 was rejected; he upped it a little and it was accepted. The following year Alexievich won the Nobel Prize in Literature and there was an eight-way auction for the US rights. The publisher aims to select works that are “innovative, imaginative, ambitious” © Wendy Huynh Today, Fitzcarraldo Editions has become a hallmark for a generation. Its signature International Klein Blue and clean cream titles include Nobel- and Pulitzer-prize winners, with authors ranging from French memoirist Annie Ernaux to New York-based war reporter Jon Lee Anderson and Hong Kong novelist Dorothy Tse. It specialises in contemporary literary fiction and long-form essays, seeking out work that is determinedly “innovative, imaginative, ambitious”, broadly kept at a 50-50 split between English language and literature in translation. Cult hits include Perfection by Vincenzo Latronico , an interrogation of millennial life; The Plague , essays on death and humanity by PEN Pinter-award-winner Jacqueline Rose; and this year’s Your Presence is a Danger to Your Life: Voices From Gaza by Samar Yazbek. A poetry list launched last year: this May, American poet Sasha Debevec-McKenney won the Dylan Thomas Prize for her debut collection Joy Is My Middle Name , while Makenna Goodman’s novel Helen of Nowhere is currently longlisted for the Booker Prize. It’s an extraordinary outcome for a house that started out with a single employee, 18 months’ funding, and the modest aim of publishing six books a year. “I feel fortunate to have started a press when I did,” says Testard with understatement when we meet in Fitzcarraldo’s offices in a former factory in Peckham Rye, south-east London. “I guess I turned up at the right time.” Fitzcarraldo founder and publisher Jacques Testard © Wendy Huynh “Fitzcarraldo is forging ahead on its own path and terms,” says Harriet Moore, literary agent at Alexander Aitken. “They have a robust commitment to the long view, a confidence in their own sensibility and vision, and their books will last. It offers a place where writers can think seriously and strangely, work against the expected, follow their obsessions, play.” “Jacques is concerned about quality, not quantity,” says Norwegian writer Jon Fosse , who won the Nobel Prize in 2023; Fitzcarraldo had published Septology , a seven-part novel in a single sentence, the previous year. “He has trusted me.” Fosse had won numerous international awards, but his prose was not published in the UK until Fitzcarraldo released Scenes from a Childhood in 2018. “Jacques is an attentive editor who gives excellent advice and is deeply respectful of authors,” says Ernaux. The Years had been published to acclaim in France in 2008 but it was not until 2018 that Fitzcarraldo published the translation to a rapturous reception, credited as contributing towards Ernaux’s 2022 Nobel win. (Testard had argued the case to nominate it for the International Booker despite it being hybrid-memoir rather than fiction; it was shortlisted.) It now seems absurd that Ernaux, Fosse and Alexievich (as well as Nobel-winner Olga Tokarczuk , whose Drive Your Plow Over the Bones of the Dead is a Fitzcarraldo bestseller) had not been published in the UK sooner. Testard shrugs when this is put to him, pointing out that when Fitzcarraldo launched there was still a tendency in bookshops to shelve international literature in its own category, “almost labelling it as a separate genre”. He attributes this partly to a British Empire legacy; that with the Commonwealth there’s “a sense that you’re [already] bringing writers in from the peripheries”. There is also the commercial aspect – “this notion that translation is more expensive, and you’ll never be able to recoup the money”. But there is also the question of discovering it in the first place. Testard grew up reading “indiscriminately” in English and French, and he also reads Spanish. “There are very, very few editors in UK publishing who read in other languages,” he says. “In Spain or France or Germany you have to have three or four languages to be in the editorial positions we are in.” At the Fitzcarraldo Editions office in Peckham, south London. From left: operations executive Samir Chadha, associate publisher Tamara Sampey-Jawad, operations director Jennifer Tighe, editor Charlotte Jackson and editor and publicist Emma Berrill © Wendy Huynh Testard, 41, possesses the extreme courtesy often typical of his generation, underscored by a certain steel. Wearing a collarless blue shirt and dark trousers, he talks fluently and rapidly about how his frustrations with the anglophone publishing industry brought him where he is today. The open-plan space, now housing 11 employees, is all white walls and deep-blue accents, light pouring in from the Crittall-style windows. On an exposed brick wall at one end of the room, trademark blue-and-white spines are lined up in rows, while in the small, bare meeting room, coloured Post-Its stuck on a wall denote the year’s publishing schedule: non-fiction, fiction, poetry, classics. Outside, over the railway line, sits Peckham Levels, the multistorey car park turned cultural hub where Fitzcarraldo holds its annual party each summer. Testard’s gravitas echoes across the house – although sometimes this effect seems almost accidental. “Can we do that?”, O’Meara recalls wondering when Testard first suggested taking the name Fitzcarraldo from Werner Herzog’s 1982 film about an opera-loving fanatic rampaging around the Peruvian jungle. Your browser does not support playing this file but you can still download the MP3 file to play locally. Labour officials in Downing Street and beyond have discussed the parameters in which a snap election could be called. Will Andy Burnham take the gamble? As speculation about the idea grips Westminster, host Lucy Fisher is joined by political editor George Parker and deputy political editor Jim Pickard to weigh up the risks and rewards of going to the public early. They also look ahead to the Labour Party conference in Liverpool starting this weekend, and the troubles that lie ahead for UK-EU relations. Plus George reports back from Burnham’s first major international summit at the UN general assembly in New York, where the prime minister weathered his first encounter with Donald Trump. Follow Lucy on X or Bluesky @LOS_Fisher , @lucyfisher.ft.com ; George on @georgewparker.bsky.social , @GeorgeWParker ; Jim @PickardJE Want more? articles.title: In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait
articles.content: In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on x (opens in a new window) In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on facebook (opens in a new window) In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on linkedin (opens in a new window) In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on whatsapp (opens in a new window) In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on x (opens in a new window) In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on facebook (opens in a new window) In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on linkedin (opens in a new window) In Rome, a palazzo becomes a self-portrait on whatsapp (opens in a new window) Maria Shollenbarger . Photography by Ramona Balaban Published September 26 2026 Jump to comments section Print this page Unlock the Editor’s Digest for free Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter. “I never really designed this space,” says 30-year-old artist and designer Paolo del Gallo di Roccagiovine. “It simply grew around my work.” We’re in an early-18th-century palazzo midway down the ruler-straight stretch of Rome’s Via del Babuino , three floors above the street’s neat ranks of artisan and designer boutiques. The grand, high-ceilinged apartment that del Gallo has welcomed me into has been owned by his family for generations; today its warren of rooms has been conscripted for his various artistic projects. A bed designed by del Gallo using a baroque headboard from the family collection © Ramona Balaban “Its last permutation was as my grandfather’s law office,” del Gallo continues. “At some point he emptied it completely, intending to figure out what to do with it at a later date.” Then Covid came. “My brother, my two sisters and I moved in very quickly to distance ourselves from our parents and grandparents.” Mattresses were thrown onto floors; in place of several of the doors, which had been sent out for restoration, del Gallo hung textiles he’d brought back from India and Uzbekistan. His siblings, he recalls, “arrived with large suitcases full of clothes. I apparently decided that my essentials for surviving lockdown were an antique gilt grotto table, a pair of beautiful chairs and some silver cutlery.” The 18th-century desk that he uses as his work table, covered in studies, drawings and raw materials © Ramona Balaban By 2022, he realised the apartment “had quietly filled itself with my things: paintings, materials, objects I’d collected”. So he came to an arrangement with his family to use it as his atelier – a place to work, receive clients and spend the occasional night in town. Del Gallo’s creative output moves between sculpture, painting, installation and interior-design intervention. Historical objects – a chair, a mirror, a book, a fragment of an ancient Ionic column capital – are “active structures” within his work. An antique hourglass is embellished with a hyperrealist rendering of an exotic butterfly; a pair of 18th-century doors are gilded in patterns like shards of light. An artwork from Paolo del Gallo’s 2025 show Butterfly Effect, along with ceramic sculptures, including one of his ancestor Zénaïde Bonaparte © Ramona Balaban His commissions range from tiny installation-like sculptures of shells and corals to entire ballrooms frescoed to residents’ specifications. Del Gallo’s work can be found across Rome: there’s a large mural inside Villa Europa, the official headquarters of the EU delegation, restoration work at the Belgian Embassy to the Quirinal and the former Belgian Embassy to the Holy See (the Belgian ambassador, Pierre-Emmanuel De Bauw, also owns his work) and pieces in private homes. At his mother’s mid-18th-century villa , the walls are covered in his dreamily atmospheric murals. Del Gallo with one of his artworks in the archive room © Ramona Balaban “What drew me to Paolo’s work was his sensitivity to nature and texture, coupled with his deep love for and integration of his own history,” says New York-based collector Tracey Hejailan-Amon. “What’s striking is how seamlessly these two registers coexist in his practice, and how easily they integrate with other artists’ works.” “Architecture is never simply a backdrop,” says del Gallo, tall and rangy, dressed in an old white button-down shirt with sleeves rolled up and loose trousers. He’s drawn to “spaces that already carry a strong sense of memory. When I work on historical surfaces, like mercury or mirror, it creates a trace that I couldn’t invent myself. I think of it as a kind of collaboration with time.” From left: a neoclassical marble oil lamp – one of his favourite pieces – painted doors he created for a 2021 exhibition at Palazzo Colonna, an oil on raw linen painting of an emu he painted while in Mexico and a door from Palazzo Sacchetti © Ramona Balaban An oil painting on an antique mirror – a work in progress © Ramona Balaban Time and history play an outsized part in del Gallo’s art. His family tree includes Napoleon Bonaparte and the Spanish royal family; he has lived most of his life in grand historic residences. His brothers and sisters pursued more conventional careers while he studied at Rome’s Accademia di Belle Arti. “I don’t remember ever deciding to be an artist,” he says. “I just grew up surrounded by art, and architecture.” At 16, he began practising restoration, which informed his later style; the natural-history books of his ancestor, ornithologist Charles-Lucien Bonaparte, “taught me very early to look closely at nature – its beauty, fragility and complexity”. He brought it permanently into his visual language. The main salon at  del Gallo’s family apartment in Rome has the original palazzo flooring and frescoes on the ceiling. He painted the mural on the walls using natural pigments such as lapis lazuli and Armenian earth © Ramona Balaban In the apartment’s main salon, “the principal theme is day and night”. A combination of stripping back layers of older paint and layering on new ones has resulted in vast semi-abstract murals of cloud and sky. On one wall, a cool white sun projects slightly from the surface; opposite, a pale moon is discernible through darker tones. Del Gallo’s delicate colours – rendered with rare materials such as lapis lazuli dust and Armenian soil – reprise the tones of the original ceiling frescoes. Two canvases, one hung midway up the wall and another leaning next to the fireplace (both unframed, as is del Gallo’s preference), echo the celestial theme at a more contained scale. The 18th-century chest of drawers in the bedroom is a Neapolitan piece. On top is a gilt crucifix from the private chapel of his family’s palace, a carved-bone pyramid and a vase he found in Mexico. He restored and painted the historic walls himself © Ramona Balaban Del Gallo’s penchant for the palimpsest has even reshaped the structure of his surroundings. “Sometimes I wake up convinced that there must be something hidden above a false ceiling, and decide to open it up. One day I imagined there was a fireplace behind a wall; I started drilling, and actually found it there, blocked up, with traces of soot inside.” Del Gallo crafted a new surround, mixing cement, lime and marble dust to create an unadorned frame that’s an elegant counterpoint to the ornate room. “I don’t only work in any one room,” says del Gallo. “It’s difficult to call a single space ‘my studio’ because in reality I make use of the whole apartment. It has become part of the creative process. Inevitably, it influences everything I do.” A corner room full of easels and tables “has the best light, and is where I store most of my materials”. A small but perfectly formed dining room, its walls hung with family porcelain, has a Carlo Scarpa table, covered in the same linen he uses for painting, at which he sometimes alights. The whole space is a locus for artistic experimentation that’s also as intimate and revealing a self-portrait as a home can be.
